## Columns: batting game logs

One row per batter per game. 41 columns. A row is identified by `game_pk` + `team_id` + `player_id`.

```{=html}
<div class="store-dict"><table class="table">
<thead><tr>
<th>Column</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>What it holds</th>
</tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>game_pk</td><td>string</td><td>MLB&#x27;s id for the game, the same id MLB.com and Baseball Savant use.</td></tr>
<tr><td>game_date</td><td>date</td><td>Official date of the game; a suspended game keeps the date it started.</td></tr>
<tr><td>season</td><td>int</td><td>Season the game belongs to, as a four-digit year.</td></tr>
<tr><td>season_type</td><td>string</td><td>regular for the regular season, postseason for every playoff round.</td></tr>
<tr><td>game_type</td><td>string</td><td>MLB game type code: R regular season, F wild card round, D division series, L league championship series, W World Series.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player_id</td><td>string</td><td>MLB (MLBAM) id of the batter.</td></tr>
<tr><td>player_name</td><td>string</td><td>Batter&#x27;s full name.</td></tr>
<tr><td>team_id</td><td>string</td><td>MLB id of the player&#x27;s or row&#x27;s team.</td></tr>
<tr><td>team</td><td>string</td><td>Team abbreviation as Baseball Savant lists the franchise today (AZ, ATH, CWS, KC, SD, SF, TB, WSH), used for every season.</td></tr>
<tr><td>team_name</td><td>string</td><td>Full team name as it was that season.</td></tr>
<tr><td>opponent_id</td><td>string</td><td>MLB id of the opposing team.</td></tr>
<tr><td>opponent</td><td>string</td><td>Opposing team&#x27;s abbreviation.</td></tr>
<tr><td>opponent_name</td><td>string</td><td>Opposing team&#x27;s full name as it was that season.</td></tr>
<tr><td>home_away</td><td>string</td><td>home when the team was the home team, away when it was the visitor.</td></tr>
<tr><td>batting_order</td><td>int</td><td>Lineup slot the player batted in, 1 through 9.</td></tr>
<tr><td>batting_order_entry</td><td>int</td><td>Order in which the player took that lineup slot: 0 for the starter, 1 for the first substitute, 2 for the next.</td></tr>
<tr><td>starter</td><td>bool</td><td>True when the player was in the starting lineup.</td></tr>
<tr><td>plate_appearances</td><td>int</td><td>Official plate appearances, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>at_bats</td><td>int</td><td>Official at-bats, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>runs</td><td>int</td><td>Runs scored, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>hits</td><td>int</td><td>Hits, counted from the play-by-play outcomes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>singles</td><td>int</td><td>Singles, counted from the play-by-play outcomes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>doubles</td><td>int</td><td>Doubles, counted from the play-by-play outcomes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>triples</td><td>int</td><td>Triples, counted from the play-by-play outcomes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>home_runs</td><td>int</td><td>Home runs, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>total_bases</td><td>int</td><td>Total bases: singles plus two per double, three per triple and four per home run in the play-by-play outcomes.</td></tr>
<tr><td>rbi</td><td>int</td><td>Runs batted in, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>walks</td><td>int</td><td>Walks, intentional walks included.</td></tr>
<tr><td>intentional_walks</td><td>int</td><td>Intentional walks drawn.</td></tr>
<tr><td>strikeouts</td><td>int</td><td>Times the batter struck out.</td></tr>
<tr><td>hit_by_pitch</td><td>int</td><td>Times hit by a pitch.</td></tr>
<tr><td>sac_flies</td><td>int</td><td>Sacrifice flies, which do not count as at-bats.</td></tr>
<tr><td>sac_bunts</td><td>int</td><td>Sacrifice bunts, which do not count as at-bats.</td></tr>
<tr><td>gidp</td><td>int</td><td>Times grounded into a double play.</td></tr>
<tr><td>stolen_bases</td><td>int</td><td>Stolen bases, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>caught_stealing</td><td>int</td><td>Times caught stealing, from the box score.</td></tr>
<tr><td>balls_in_play</td><td>int</td><td>Plate appearances that ended with the ball put in play, home runs included.</td></tr>
<tr><td>avg_exit_velocity</td><td>float</td><td>Average exit velocity in miles per hour of the balls in play Statcast tracked; blank when none was tracked.</td></tr>
<tr><td>max_exit_velocity</td><td>float</td><td>Highest exit velocity in miles per hour among the balls in play Statcast tracked; blank when none was tracked.</td></tr>
<tr><td>hard_hit</td><td>int</td><td>Balls in play with an exit velocity of 95 miles per hour or more.</td></tr>
<tr><td>barrels</td><td>int</td><td>Balls in play Statcast classes as barrels, its best combination of exit velocity and launch angle.</td></tr>
</tbody></table></div>
```

## Columns: pitching game logs

One row per pitcher per game. 35 columns. A row is identified by `game_pk` + `player_id`.

```{=html}

<thead><tr>
<th>Column</th>

<th>What it holds</th>

<tr><td>runs_while_pitching</td><td>int</td><td>Runs the opponent scored while this pitcher was on the mound; a runner left on base by an earlier pitcher counts here, so this is not runs charged or earned runs.</td></tr>
<tr><td>balls_in_play</td><td>int</td><td>Plate appearances that ended with the ball put in play, home runs included.</td></tr>
<tr><td>avg_exit_velocity</td><td>float</td><td>Average exit velocity in miles per hour of the balls in play Statcast tracked; blank when none was tracked.</td></tr>
```

## Source and method

Plate appearances, at-bats, runs, home runs, RBI and steals are the official box score figures from the MLB Stats API (schedule, box scores, linescores, game notes). Hits by type, walks, strikeouts and every pitching line are counted from Baseball Savant Statcast pitch data and match the play-by-play file row for row; a few dozen plate appearances a season in 2017 and 2018 have no recorded outcome there and are missing from those counts. Earned runs, runs charged, wins, losses, saves, holds and fielding are not included because they cannot be derived exactly from these sources. A player who appeared without batting, scoring or attempting a steal has no batting row.

The same file layout, IDs and column names are used for every season, so seasons stack without cleanup. See [how the store works](help.qmd) for formats, delivery and the license.

## More MLB data

[Team Game Logs](mlb-team-logs.qmd) · [Play-by-Play](mlb-play-by-play.qmd) · [Games and Results](mlb-schedule.qmd) · [All MLB data](mlb.qmd)

::: {.faq-item}
### How do the MLB files join to each other?

On the ID columns. Game, team and player IDs are the same strings in every MLB file and every season, so a join on `game_id` (plus `team` or `player_id` where the grain needs it) lines them up.
:::

::: {.faq-item}
### Which games are included?

Every regular-season and postseason game, built from the official game feeds and Statcast. Regular season and postseason sit in the same file, told apart by `season_type`. Preseason and All-Star games are left out.
:::
